newsitem.title: BELGIUM: RENAULT WORKERS ANNOUNCE NEW EU DAY OF ACTION.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT WORKERS ANNOUNCE NEW EU DAY OF ACTION.

text.p: Employees of French carmaker Renault have declared Friday April 4 as a new European day of action in protest at planned closures and job losses.
As part of the day of action the unions representing the workers will hold simultaneous press conferences in Brussels, Paris and Madrid, the unions said in a statement.

The workers at Renault's plant at Vilvoorde in Belgium have been up in arms since the company's shock announcement on February 27 that it woulkd close down the profitable factory in July with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
Nearly 3,000 job losses have also been announced in France. Renault said last week it lost 5.25 billion French francs in 1996.

Renault workers have staged sporadic protest actions in Belgium and France -- including leading the estimated 70,000 people who flocked to Brussels from all over Europe 10 days ago to join a mass March for Jobs.

Although the march was aimed primarily at the failure of European Union governments to create jobs as they slash budgets and raise taxes in preparation for joining the bloc's single currency in 1999, the Renault case has focused attention.
On Monday some 250 Vilvoorde workers briefly blocked the departure from Brussels South Station of the Eurostar train to London.
The Belgian government and the unions have threatened to take Renault to court over the manner in which it announced the Vilvoorde closure decision.
Under EU law a company must consult its employees over any major strategic decisions -- particularly concerning jobs. Renault did not do so.
